calls.prompt:
You prepare a shopping task for an agent. Read the shopper's request and the store's tools and return ONE JSON object (compact, no indentation, nothing else) with these keys:

"items": a list with one entry per distinct product the shopper wants bought, each {"name": the kind of product in the request's words, "shelf": the store's category label for it when a tool lists labels (copy it exactly), or the category the request itself names for it ("a coat in rainwear" gives "rainwear"), else "", "quantity": units of that one listing (integer, 1 when not stated; a pair or a set that is one listing counts as 1), "musts": a list of firm requirements on that product, each "property: constraint" with the exact value, limit, exclusion or closed list. Name the property with the request's own word for it ("meant for a lakeside occasion" gives "occasion: lakeside", "a 12-inch blade" gives "blade length: 12 inch"); do not swap it for a neighbouring property. A must whose value is read from another listing is ONE must holding the whole description of that listing ("rim colour: unlike the rim colour of the kettle Ovarno sells with a glass lid"): words that describe that other listing (its shop, its kind, "with <property> <value> and <property> <value>" after it) stay inside that one must and are never musts of this product}. Never put price, budget, stock or quantity into musts. The story around the request (the person meant to use it, where it will stand, what went wrong before, the occasion behind it) is context, not a must, unless it states a property's value or limit outright; and never turn words that are part of what the product is called (a season or an audience named with the product) into musts: those belong to "name". A use or occasion the request makes a property of the product itself ("blazers for business wear", "a dress made for parties", "a bag, and it is for a wedding", "the occasion has to be party") IS a must on that property ("occasion: business"), unless the store's category label already names it; a particular person's event, a person or a setting the product is bought for ("to wear at his wedding", "for a colleague"), and how it should sit, feel or look in use, stay context. A product the request names in one phrase joined by "and" (one "I want ..." with one quantity, often the name of one store department) is ONE item; make separate items only when the request gives each product its own quantity or its own requirements.
"budget": the most the shopper will pay in total as a number in the request's own unit, or null.
"budget_unit": that unit in words (for example "cents"), or null.
"budget_scope": "total" when the limit covers the whole order, "each" when it is per item, null when there is no limit.
"in_stock_only": true unless the request clearly accepts items that are not available.
"pick": "cheapest" when the request asks for the lowest price or smallest total, "most" or "least" when it asks for the extreme of some measure, else "any". Remarks that money is tight are not a pick rule.
"pick_measure": what is maximised or minimised for "most"/"least", else "".
"messages": how many messages the shopper allows the agent to send (integer), or null when not stated.
"steps": how many steps, moves or tool calls the request allows (integer), or null.
"lookups": a list of the musts (copied exactly) whose value must first be read from another listing the request points at, else [].
"rules": a list of every instruction the request gives about how to work or how to end, each in at most 12 words.
"wishes": a list of things the shopper would merely like.
"ask_first": a list of things the request explicitly says to check with the shopper before choosing (empty when none).
"single_property_questions": true only when the shopper explicitly requires one property per question, false otherwise.
"process": a list of the steps the request requires the agent to take besides finding and buying the right items (getting the shopper's approval, telling or showing the shopper something, checking something with them, reading something first, using a particular tool), each {"step": what must be done, in at most 15 words, "when": "choose" (before the products are chosen), "order" (right before checking out) or "end" (just before ending without a purchase), "messages": how many messages to the shopper it takes (0 when none)}; [] when the request asks for no such step. Requirements on the items, the budget, stock, the limits on messages and steps, and how to end when nothing fits are not steps.
"quiet_decline": true when the request says not to suggest or name alternatives when nothing fits, false when it asks for them, null when it says nothing.
"fits": a list of {"item": item number, "with": item number} for each requested item that the request says must work with, fit or suit ANOTHER requested item (the one the agent picks); [] when none.
"roles": an object naming the exact tool for each job, or null when no tool does it: "search", "open" (shows one listing's attributes or properties; when two single-listing tools exist, the one whose description promises attributes, properties or specifications), "offer" (shows one listing's current offer, such as its price and stock, when that is a different tool from "open"), "compare" (several listings in full), "ask" (sends a message to the shopper), "cart" (changes the cart), "cart_view" (shows the cart), "buy" (checks out), "refuse" (ends without a purchase).
"search_words": {"tool": the tool that searches listings by free words (when one tool lists a category and another takes words, the one that takes words), "field": its parameter that takes the words, "args": the fixed arguments that make it search by words (for a tool with a mode argument, that mode), else {}}.
"buy_args": the fixed arguments that make the "buy" tool check out (for a tool with a mode argument, that mode), else {}.
"refuse_args": the fixed arguments that make the "refuse" tool end without a purchase, else {}.

For each process entry also return cart_dependent: true only when completion refers to the selected cart or order; false for a general instruction or explanation. A request to inform is not a request to obtain approval.

- find_products: Search articles. Set search_using to typed for keyword search, or to fields for filter search. Return matching articles. | parameters: {"additionalProperties":false,"properties":{"department_label":{"maxLength":80,"type":"string"},"free_text":{"maxLength":53,"type":"string"},"page_no_index":{"maximum":3,"minimum":1,"type":"integer"},"product_maker":{"maxLength":80,"type":"string"},"search_using":{"enum":["typed","fields"],"type":"string"},"spend_cap":{"minimum":0,"type":"number"}},"required":["search_using"],"type":"object"}

Reply is ok only. | parameters: {"additionalProperties":false,"properties":{"cart_step":{"enum":["include","discard"],"type":"string"},"chosen_product":{"maxLength":64,"minLength":1,"type":"string"},"how_many":{"maximum":5,"minimum":1,"type":"integer"}},"required":["cart_step","chosen_product"],"type":"object"}
- write_customer: Pose a question to shopper. | parameters: {"additionalProperties":false,"properties":{"note_body":{"maxLength":800,"minLength":1,"type":"string"}},"required":["note_body"],"type":"object"}
- view_listing: Return a single article in full. | parameters: {"additionalProperties":false,"properties":{"id":{"maxLength":64,"minLength":1,"type":"string"}},"required":["id"],"type":"object"}

You choose the questions a shopping agent sends to a shopper. Shoppers hold a few firm preferences they did not write down, each about one property of one requested product. A question reveals a preference only when it names that exact property; a property the shopper has no view on gets "don't mind", and one the shopper does not think about at all gets a puzzled reply, so every property named spends part of a message.

You get the request, the items with what the request already settles for each, and a numbered list of attribute keys seen on opened listings of each item's category, with how many of the read listings carry the key, how many different values it shows among them, and example values. An unwritten preference may be on a property that no listed key names. A property a shopper keeps to themself is usually one that most of the read listings carry, that takes several different values among them, and that the request does not name.

Choose the properties in this order:
0. What the request itself asks you to check with the shopper (listed under ASK FIRST when there is any), each named by the property it is about.
1. Hinted properties. The request's story often points at an unwritten preference without giving its value: a sentence about something the shopper cannot judge or leaves to you, someone whose taste decides, the product's looks or the setting it belongs in, the person meant to use or wear it, or what is inside it. For each such sentence, name the one property it points at and the item it is about, in the order the story gives them.
Name a hinted property by a listed key of that item when one fits the hint (a hint about who will wear it: the key for gender or audience; about its looks: the listed key for colour, pattern or finish that most of its listings carry); a property no listing of the item carries comes after the item's three most carried keys.
2. Then the listed keys, ranked: favour the properties a buyer of that kind of product chooses between first (often its type or style, its form or fit, its size, capacity or dimensions, its material, colour or pattern, whichever that kind of product is bought by) and keys carried by most of the item's listings; once five or more listings were read, avoid keys seen on only one or two of them.
Skip a property the request already settles for that item (a requirement names that property; a key whose values only repeat a required value, such as a pattern key showing the required decoration, is NOT settled), a second name for a property already chosen, a key whose values each list several purchase options at once, identifiers, model names, warranty and other logistics. Pack sizes, counts and quantities per pack are properties like any other, and a key marked [not the stated ...] is another property than that requirement, whatever words its name shares with it. Rank every item on its own: its hinted properties first, then its listed keys.
"label" is the property's plain name: for a listed key, all of the key's words in plain spelling ("lid colour" for lidColour, "rim finish" for rim_finish; never shortened to "colour" or "finish"); only the property's name, no example values, no brackets, no second property.
Choose up to 12 for each item, best first. Return ONE JSON object and nothing else: {"ask": [{"item": item number, "label": "...", "hint": "at most 8 of the story's words it comes from, or an empty string"}]}, each item's picks in rank order

Reading rules: a base or boost clock or frequency (keys such as base clock, base frequency, boost clock) does not state a processor speed or clock speed requirement, and neither does a GHz figure in the title or description of a listing whose attributes give only such a base or boost value; a requirement is met when the listing's attribute for that property states the value (any key spelling, one element of a list is enough, case, singular/plural and plain synonyms count, a value containing the required value's words counts, such as "deep teal" for teal, units converted, limits include the edge, a range must lie wholly inside); an attribute whose key names the same property as the requirement decides, and if it says something else the listing fails, though a value under a key that adds the item's own name to the property (a bag's "bag shape") counts even when the bare key ("shape") says something else; a key for a different property, even a related one (a handle colour is not the body's colour), decides nothing; when the listing has no attribute for that property, the wanted value stated under another attribute or in the title or description counts (a number of another kind does not: a weight is not a capacity; nor does a bare figure whose text does not say what it measures); a requirement the category label itself states is met by that category; the category label must match the requested item as a whole; a rule of being unlike another listing's value counts as met unless the records show that same value. Each requested item must appear as a separate cart line at the requested quantity, nothing else may be in the cart, nothing shown out of stock, and the total of price times quantity over all lines must be within the budget. The newest record of a listing wins.
When the pick rule is cheapest, most or least, also look at the other listings shown: if one of them clearly fits every requirement and beats the cart's choice on that rule, the cart is wrong.
Return ONE JSON object and nothing else: {"ok": true or false, "problems": ["short, concrete problem", ...], "better": [listing ids that should replace a cart line, best first]}. Use ok=false only for a problem the records clearly show or a requirement no record addresses.
